declarations.description:
Turns keyboard shortcuts into events. One element holds every shortcut of an application (or of a region) in
its `bindings` list and renders nothing. When a binding's keys are pressed the element calls `preventDefault()`
on the key event, fires `shortcut` with the binding's `action`, then runs the binding's `handler` and activates
its `for` target, unless the event was cancelled.

Every key must be composed with Ctrl, ⌘ or Alt (`mod+k`, `alt+1`, `mod+k mod+s`); only Escape and F1–F24 may be
bound on their own, and those are ignored while the user types in a field unless `allowInInputs` is set. A binding's `scope` limits it to focus inside the element's parent (`parent`) or inside any element matching
a CSS selector; when several bindings match, the most narrowly scoped wins, across every `c2-shortcut` on the page.
A key a component has already handled (`preventDefault()` on it) is left alone.
declarations.name: Shortcut

members.name: entries
members.description: Every binding with its platform-aware display labels, for a cheatsheet or a command palette.

members.name: syncAriaKeyShortcuts
members.description: Announce each `for` target's shortcut, leaving any `aria-keyshortcuts` the author wrote untouched.

events.name: shortcut
events.description: Fired when a binding's keys are pressed. `detail.action` is the binding's `action`, `detail.keys` the alternative that matched, `detail.binding` the binding and `detail.originalEvent` the `keydown`. Cancelable: `preventDefault()` skips the binding's `handler` and `for` target. Does not bubble.

declarations.description:
The keyboard-shortcuts sheet, the dialog a "?" key opens on GitHub or Gmail: every shortcut of the page grouped
by section, each key drawn with `c2-kbd`, and a search field that filters them.

The sheet reads the bindings of the `c2-shortcut` elements in its document (or shadow root), or of those `for`
names, each time it opens: a binding is listed when it has a `description`, under its `group`. `shortcuts` adds
entries the page does not bind itself, such as a component's own arrow keys; they are listed after the bindings.
A disabled binding or `c2-shortcut` is left out, and `no-bindings` lists `shortcuts` alone. Shortcuts with no group
come first, under "General" when others have a group.

Open it with `show()`, the `open` attribute, the sheet's own `keys` (`keys="mod+/"`), or a button with
`commandfor="<sheet id>" command="--show"` (`--toggle`, `--hide`). The dialog is a `c2-modal`, loaded with the
rest of the sheet the first time it opens; `inline` lists the shortcuts in the page instead, for a help or settings
page. The `footer` slot is an action zone for the app's own links ("Customize shortcuts").

members.name: inline
members.description: List the shortcuts in the page, without a dialog.

members.name: for
members.description: Space-separated ids of the `c2-shortcut` elements to read. Empty: every `c2-shortcut` in the sheet's document or shadow root.

members.name: shortcuts
members.description: Shortcuts listed after the bindings: `{ keys, description, group? }` objects, or a JSON array as an attribute.

members.name: noBindings
members.description: List `shortcuts` only, without reading any `c2-shortcut`: a help panel for a component's own keys.

members.name: keys
members.description: Keys that toggle the dialog, in the `c2-shortcut` syntax (`mod+/`; Ctrl, ⌘ or Alt required, as for a binding). Listed in the sheet itself; ignored by an `inline` sheet.

members.name: renderItem
members.description: Draws the content of each row instead of the description and the keys.

members.name: toggle
members.description: Opens the dialog when it is closed, closes it when it is open.

members.name: refresh
members.description: Reads the `c2-shortcut` bindings again, after they changed while the sheet is shown.
